items.title: Angry Venezuelans accuse government of negligence over earthquake response
items.description: People in areas devastated by twin earthquakes say they need more support from the government.

items.title: Aftershock frays nerves as many Venezuelans left to fend for themselves
items.description: In areas devastated by the twin earthquakes, people are using crowbars, pickaxes and their bare hands to try to reach survivors.

items.title: Founder of Asian super-app Gojek sentenced to years in jail for corruption
items.description: The case against Gojek founder Nadiem Makarim relates to a laptop deal made during his term as Indonesia's education minister.

items.title: Heavy security in South Africa as anti-migrant protesters take to the streets
items.description: Thousands of people have left South Africa ahead of Tuesday's deadline set by anti-migrant groups.

items.title: Manhunt under way after bomb injures Ukrainian oligarch and family in Monaco
items.description: The blast was caused by an explosive device which appeared to contain bolts and pellets, the head of Monaco's government said.

items.title: One big win and three defeats for Trump in dramatic day at Supreme Court
items.description: While Trump celebrated a ruling expanding presidential power to remove and replace regulators, other decisions were major setbacks.

items.title: Chinese tycoon sentenced to 30 years in US jail
items.description: Guo Wengui branded himself as a China critic, gaining followers who backed his fraudulent schemes.

items.title: Osaka pays 'love and respect to Japan' in Wimbledon kimono
items.description: Naomi Osaka has long been renowned for dazzling crowds with her on-court outfits - but making that compatible with Wimbledon's all-white dress code required special inspiration.

items.title: US says it has agreed to 'stand down' after exchange of strikes with Iran
items.description: A series of strikes over the weekend saw the US and Iran accuse each other of violating the ceasefire agreement.

items.title: Pakistani strikes kill at least 28 civilians in Afghanistan, UN says
items.description: Pakistan claims it was targeting militants near its border, but the Taliban government calls it an "atrocity".

items.title: Six people shot dead at centre for mothers and children in Germany
items.description: The male suspect who has been arrested was in a custody dispute over his baby daughter, police say.

items.title: Putin makes rare admission of fuel shortages caused by Ukrainian strikes
items.description: The Russian president acknowledged Ukraine's attacks were "obviously creating problems" but denied the shortages were "critical".
